title: Partial schema reconciliation and tool-call metrics acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define acceptance criteria, tests, and rollout guidance for handling partially-emitted structured outputs during streaming responses and for surfacing reliable tool/function-call metrics. Goal: ensure consumer apps can safely reconcile incrementally-emitted objects, detect schema drift mid-stream, and get robust metrics for tool invocation correctness and latency.
background: Users are integrating function/tool calling with streaming LLM responses. In production we see partial objects (incomplete JSON fragments), schema churn between model versions, and ambiguous tool-target selections mid-stream. Current behavior can cause consumer crashes, duplicated tool invocations, or silent failures. This ticket consolidates requirements for a deterministic reconciliation protocol, explicit stream-level metadata events, and bounded metrics for tool calls.
scope: Acceptance criteria and test harness for: (1) schema-announcement and schema-rebase events in the stream, (2) rules for reconciling partial objects into final canonical objects, (3) tool-call idempotency signals and metrics (attempts, latency, success/failure), (4) backwards compatibility with clients that do not understand schema-announcements.
out_of_scope: Changes to model training/finetuning to eliminate schema drift, SDK implementation work (implementation tickets will be separate), backend billing changes for additional telemetry storage.
acceptance_criteria: Schema-announcement event: Every streaming response that intends to emit structured objects must include an initial 'schema-announcement' event within the first 3 chunks. The event MUST declare a stable schema_id and a minimal JSON Schema pointer (or URL). If no schema is declared, consumer must treat stream as unstructured text.

Progressive object emission: Partial object fragments are allowed but MUST be wrapped by explicit 'object-start' / 'object-chunk' / 'object-end' markers in the stream. The client can safely perform incremental parsing and must be able to choose to act on 'object-end' only. The runtime will guarantee that markers are emitted in-order and non-overlapping for a single logical object.

Schema rebase: If the model changes the schema mid-stream, it MUST emit a 'schema-rebase' event that includes previous_schema_id and new_schema_id. The server will also emit a reconciliation hint describing backward-compatibility (compatible | additive | breaking). Consumers may choose whether to continue parsing new objects based on that hint.

Final object canonicalization: When 'object-end' is emitted, the runtime MUST validate the assembled object against the current schema_id. If validation fails and the failure is fixable by a deterministic correction (e.g., unquoted string, trailing comma), the runtime will attempt one correction and include a 'correction-applied' flag and diff in the stream. If validation fails otherwise, runtime emits 'object-error' with failure reason and guidance (reject | best-effort | accept-partial).

Idempotent tool-calls: Tool/function call events contain a call_id (UUID) and a call_intent_hash. The runtime and client must use call_id for deduplication. If a call_id is re-sent due to re-stream or retry, the tool backend must treat it as the same logical invocation and return cached results if within TTL. Acceptance requires demo with duplicate chunk replay without duplicate side-effects.

Tool-call metrics completeness: For every tool invocation surfaced in a session, the system must emit metrics: tool_call.invocations (count), tool_call.success_rate, tool_call.latency_p50/95/99, tool_call.duplicate_retries. These metrics must be available at the route/model level in Console with <1 minute latency for dashboards.

Partial finalization semantics: Streams that end unexpectedly (network cutoff) must mark any in-flight object with 'object-truncated' and include last_valid_offset. Consumers must not assume completeness of objects without 'object-end'. Acceptance requires simulated network cutoff tests where consumer does not crash and reports a recoverable truncated-object event.

Backwards compatibility: Clients that do not recognize 'schema-announcement' or object markers must still receive deterministic text output. Server must provide a 'compat-mode' toggle on the response envelope that, when enabled, duplicates the structured emission into a best-effort text appendix at stream end. Acceptance requires no change in non-upgraded SDKs and explicit 'compat-mode' opt-in for legacy flows.

Operational alerts: If tool_call.duplicate_retries exceeds configured threshold (default 3) for a tenant in 1 minute, system must trigger an SRE alert and flag the tenant in Console with a notice and suggested mitigations.

Privacy & PII: Tool-call telemetry must not include PII or prompt content. Acceptance requires automated lint in ingestion pipeline that redacts prompt text from telemetry streams and a manual spot-check of 50 samples showing zero prompt leakage.
test_cases: End-to-end streaming test: client subscribes to stream; server emits schema-announcement, emits three objects (one with a mid-stream schema-rebase to additive fields), verify client assembles 3 canonical objects and tool_call metrics reflect 3 invocations.

Duplicate replay test: replay same chunks twice with identical call_id; verify tool backend receives single side-effect and client receives cached response second time; dashboard metrics show duplicate_retries=1 for that call_id.

Truncation simulation: drop TCP connection before object-end; consumer receives object-truncated with last_valid_offset and does not crash; object is flagged as incomplete in Console with link to relevant session trace.
Validation fail and correction: emit object with trailing comma; runtime auto-corrects, emits correction-applied with diff; final validated object accepted and stored in event log.

Legacy client compatibility: use an SDK that ignores markers; verify response readable as plain text and no API error returned when compat-mode not set; when compat-mode enabled, verify text appendix at stream end.
Telemetry PII audit: run ingestion lint on 50 sessions and confirm prompt_content fields are redacted in tool_call telemetry entries.
monitoring_and_metrics: Expose per-route tool_call.* metrics (invocations, success_rate, latencies, duplicate_retries) to Console and metrics endpoint.
Add histogram for object-reconciliation-duration (time between first object chunk and object-end canonicalization).
Surface schema-rebase frequency per model and per-tenant; high frequency (> 10% of sessions) flags for review.
Add sampling traces for streams that triggered correction-applied or object-error to speed root-cause analysis.
Retention: telemetry for tool calls retained for 90 days by default; sensitive fields redacted at ingestion.
dependencies: ENG-49210 (runtime: add explicit stream-marker wire protocol)
ENG-49821 (telemetry: redact prompt content at ingestion)
ENG-50233 (console: new per-route tool_call metrics panels)
DES-1102 (design: user-facing labels for truncated/incomplete objects in Console)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embedding full JSON Schema increases payload size; opted for schema_id + URL to a compact JSON Schema registry, with optional inline minimal schema for latency-sensitive flows.

We debated automatic corrections vs. strict rejection. Chosen approach: 1 best-effort deterministic correction with explicit correction-applied event; reduces client churn while keeping server predictable.

Rollout recommendation: feature-flag schema-announcement and object-markers behind runtime flag; run for 50% of new sign-ups for 2 weeks, monitor correction-applied rates and rebase frequency before full rollout.
SDK implications: older SDKs should ignore unknown event types; new SDKs will expose high-level helpers to subscribe to object lifecycle events.
Consider adding a lightweight 'schema_preview' API to allow clients to fetch schema by schema_id for validation prior to streaming sessions; engineered as a follow-up if adoption warrants.
decision_log: 2025-02-13: Decided on explicit markers (object-start/object-chunk/object-end) instead of relying on heuristic JSON parsing to avoid parser divergence across languages. - Asha
2025-02-15: Opted for single deterministic correction rule set (whitespace/unquoted-strings/trailing-commas) rather than arbitrary repairs. - Liam
2025-02-18: Required call_id + call_intent_hash for idempotency; tooling teams will implement dedupe cache with 5 minute default TTL. - Eng Leads
